_doc: Norway, written by hand for the recommended trips (Manu, 2026-11-16): summer in the fjords and Lofoten, winter for the northern lights in the north. Sources per area; scores on docs/RANKING.md.

areas.season: June to August are long and mild (20-22 °C, light until 23:00). December to February are dark and below freezing, with snow for the ski trails above the city.
areas.sleep: The centre between the harbour (Aker Brygge) and Karl Johans gate; Grünerløkka for cafés.

items.name: Opera roof, Akershus Fortress and the harbour
items.why: Walk up the sloping marble roof of the Opera House over the fjord, then the medieval fortress on the point and the harbour of Aker Brygge.

items.name: Vigeland Park
items.why: Over 200 granite and bronze sculptures by one man, Gustav Vigeland, around the Monolith of 121 bodies; free and open all day.

items.name: Bygdøy: the Fram and Kon-Tiki museums
items.why: Board the Fram, the wooden ship of Nansen and Amundsen's polar voyages, and see Heyerdahl's balsa raft Kon-Tiki next door; ferry from the City Hall pier in summer, bus all year.

items.name: MUNCH: The Scream and the painter's life
items.why: The museum on the harbour holds the largest Edvard Munch collection in the world, with versions of The Scream shown in turns.

items.name: Holmenkollen ski jump
items.why: Metro line 1 climbs to the ski jump over the city; the ski museum and the jump tower look down on the whole Oslofjord.

areas.season: One of Europe's wettest cities: rain on about 200 days a year, mild all year (0-3 °C in winter, 15-18 °C in summer). May to September have the long days.
areas.sleep: Near Bryggen and the fish market, or Nordnes for quiet streets.

items.name: Bryggen and the fish market
items.why: The wooden wharf of the Hanseatic merchants, on UNESCO's list, with its leaning alleys and the Hanseatic Museum, then fish soup at the market.

items.name: Fløibanen funicular and the lakes on Fløyen
items.why: Eight minutes up to 320 m for the view over the city and its fjords, then forest paths and small lakes on top, and down on foot.

items.name: Vidden: Ulriken to Fløyen over the mountains
items.why: Bergen's classic ridge walk: up Ulriken by cable car or on foot, then across open mountain above the city to Fløyen.

items.name: Fjord cruise to Mostraumen
items.why: A boat from the fish market into the narrow Osterfjord, close under waterfalls, to the tidal strait of Mostraumen and back.

areas.season: The fjord boats and the Flåm Railway run all year. May to September for walking; in winter snow lies above the fjord and some upper roads close.
areas.sleep: Flåm by the quay, or quieter Aurland 10 km along the fjord.

items.name: Nærøyfjord by boat, Flåm to Gudvangen
items.why: The narrowest arm of the Sognefjord, on UNESCO's list: 250 m wide in places under walls 1,700 m high, past the farms of Undredal and Dyrdal.

items.name: The Flåm Railway to Myrdal and back
items.why: Twenty kilometres and 865 m of climb in an hour, through 20 tunnels and past the Kjosfossen waterfall; one of the steepest normal railways in the world.

items.name: Stegastein viewpoint
items.why: A wooden platform that juts out 650 m above the Aurlandsfjord, a short drive or bus above Aurland.

items.name: Aurlandsdalen, the valley walk
items.why: Norway's 'Grand Canyon': a valley walk past waterfalls and old summer farms from Østerbø down towards Vassbygdi, bus at both ends.

items.name: Kayak on the Aurlandsfjord
items.why: A guided paddle from Flåm on still water under the fjord walls; seals and waterfalls close up.

areas.season: Fruit trees blossom along the fjord in May. Trolltunga is a summer hike, about June to mid-September; outside that only with a guide.
areas.sleep: Odda for Trolltunga (the trailhead is above Tyssedal), Lofthus or Eidfjord for the fjord.

items.name: Trolltunga
items.book: Parking at Skjeggedal or Mågelitopp, book ahead in summer
items.why: The 'troll's tongue', a flat slab of rock jutting 700 m above lake Ringedalsvatnet: one of Norway's hardest famous hikes, about 27 km return.

items.name: Vøringsfossen and the edge of Hardangervidda
items.why: A 163 m free fall into the Måbødalen gorge, seen from platforms and a step bridge, by the road up from Eidfjord.

items.name: Orchards and cider farms of Ullensvang
items.why: A quarter of Norway's fruit grows along this fjord: cider and apple juice tastings at farms between Lofthus and Utne.

areas.season: Mild and wet. Preikestolen and the Lysefjord boats are best May to September; Kjerag's road opens about June to September.
areas.sleep: Old Stavanger by the harbour; for Preikestolen, the lodge at the trailhead.

items.name: Preikestolen, the Pulpit Rock
items.best: Early or late, to miss the crowds
items.why: A flat cliff top 604 m straight above the Lysefjord, about 8 km return with 500 m of climb on stone steps.

items.name: Lysefjord cruise
items.why: From Stavanger under Preikestolen, past the Hengjanefossen waterfall and the Vagabond's Cave, with the cliff seen from below.

items.name: Old Stavanger and the harbour
items.why: About 170 white wooden houses of the 18th and 19th century on cobbled lanes, the best kept in Northern Europe.

items.name: Kjerag and the boulder
items.why: A boulder wedged in a crack 1,000 m above the Lysefjord; a steep route with chains over three ridges from Øygardsstøl, 2.5 h by car.

areas.season: June to September. The Skylift runs most of the year, but the walks on top and the glacier arms are summer outings.
areas.sleep: Loen by the fjord, or Olden.

items.name: Briksdalsbreen glacier
items.why: An arm of Jostedalsbreen, mainland Europe's biggest glacier, at the end of a path past a roaring waterfall; the ice has shrunk back a long way.

items.name: Loen Skylift to Mount Hoven
items.why: A cable car from the fjord to 1,011 m in five minutes, then paths on the summit plateau over the Nordfjord.

items.name: Lake Lovatnet to Kjenndalsbreen
items.why: A green glacier lake under 1,500 m walls, the road along it to the Kjenndal glacier, and the sites of the 1905 and 1936 rockslide waves.

areas.season: The fjord boats run all year; the mountain road over Dalsnibba opens about late May to October and Trollstigen about June to October.
areas.sleep: Geiranger at the head of the fjord.

items.name: Geirangerfjord by boat to Hellesylt
items.why: UNESCO's fjord: the Seven Sisters falls on one side, the Suitor on the other, and abandoned farms on the ledges above the water.

items.name: Skageflå farm on the cliff
items.why: Up from the fjord (boat to the landing) to a mountain farm perched 250 m above the water, then over to Homlong.

items.name: Dalsnibba and Flydalsjuvet
items.why: A road to 1,500 m with the fjord far below, and on the way down the overhanging rock of Flydalsjuvet.

items.name: Storseterfossen, walking behind the waterfall
items.why: A path from the village up to a waterfall you can walk behind, with the fjord in view.

areas.season: Romsdalseggen and Trollstigen are summer only (about June to September). The Rauma Railway runs all year.

items.name: Romsdalseggen ridge
items.book: Bus to the trailhead in Vengedalen
items.why: A narrow ridge from Vengedalen back down to Åndalsnes, with the Troll Wall and the Romsdalsfjord either side: Norway's finest day walk for many.

items.name: Rampestreken viewpoint
items.why: Sherpa steps from town to a steel platform over the valley and fjord at 550 m, or the gondola up Nesaksla.

items.name: Trollstigen road and Trollveggen
items.why: Eleven hairpins up a wall to the viewing platforms over the falls, and on the way the Troll Wall, Europe's tallest vertical rock face.

items.name: The Rauma Railway
items.why: The line from Åndalsnes up Romsdalen to Bjorli and back, past the Troll Wall and over the Kylling bridge.

areas.season: Mild and wet on the open coast. May to September for the islands and the boats.
areas.sleep: In the Art Nouveau centre by Brosundet.

items.name: Art Nouveau town and Aksla viewpoint
items.why: Rebuilt in stone after the fire of 1904 with towers and turrets, seen whole from Fjellstua after 418 steps up the hill of Aksla.

items.name: Runde, the bird island
items.why: About 100,000 pairs of seabirds nest on the cliffs, puffins from April to August; a walk up from the harbour.

areas.season: Midnight sun about 28 May to 14 July; northern lights September to March; cod fishing and drying racks February to April. The mountain paths are icy in winter.
areas.sleep: Rorbuer (red fishermen's cabins) in Reine, Hamnøy or Sakrisøy.

items.name: Reinebringen
items.why: Nearly 2,000 stone steps laid by Nepali Sherpas up to 448 m, for the famous view over Reine and its fjords.

items.name: Ryten and Kvalvika beach
items.why: A wild white beach between peaks, seen from the overhang of Ryten 543 m above the Atlantic.

items.name: Hamnøy, Reine and Å
items.why: Red cabins on stilts, cod drying on wooden racks, and the stockfish museum at Å at the end of the road.

items.name: Nusfjord fishing village
items.why: One of Norway's oldest and best kept fishing villages, with its old general store and cod-liver oil factory.

items.name: Northern lights by the fjords
items.why: Away from the lights of the villages the aurora shines over peaks and still water; best on clear nights September to March.

areas.season: Midnight sun about 28 May to 14 July; northern lights September to March; the cod season February to April.
areas.sleep: Svolvær harbour, or a rorbu in Henningsvær.

items.name: Henningsvær
items.why: A fishing village on skerries, with galleries, cafés and its football pitch on the rocks.

items.name: Trollfjord boat and sea eagles
items.why: A boat into a fjord 100 m wide under walls 1,000 m high, with white-tailed eagles fed close by.

items.name: Lofotr Viking Museum at Borg
items.why: The rebuilt 83 m longhouse of a Viking chief, found by a farmer's plough in 1983.

items.name: Haukland and Uttakleiv beaches
items.why: White sand and green water under the peaks, joined by an old road around Mannen.

items.name: Northern lights
items.why: On clear nights from September to March, from the beaches or a guided chase by minibus.

areas.season: Midnight sun late May to late July. The mountain paths are summer only; in winter, northern lights and snow down to the sea.
areas.sleep: Hamn i Senja, Mefjordvær or the fishing villages of the north coast; a car is needed.

items.name: Segla
items.why: A fin of rock 639 m straight above the Mefjord, seen best from the neighbouring top of Hesten.

items.name: The north coast road: Bergsbotn and Tungeneset
items.why: A National Tourist Route along the outer coast, with platforms over the Bergsfjord and the jagged Devil's Teeth at Tungeneset.

items.name: Northern lights over the fjords
items.why: Few people and little light: on clear nights September to March the aurora over the peaks.

areas.season: Polar night about 27 November to 15 January (blue light at midday); northern lights September to early April; whales in the fjords about November to January; midnight sun 20 May to 22 July.
areas.sleep: The centre around Storgata and the harbour.

items.name: Northern lights chase
items.why: Guides drive towards the clear sky, sometimes into Finland, to find the aurora; best September to March.

items.name: Fjellheisen cable car and the Arctic Cathedral
items.why: The white triangles of the Arctic Cathedral across the bridge, then the cable car to Storsteinen at 421 m over the city and the island.

items.name: Whale safari
items.why: Orcas and humpbacks follow the herring into the fjords north of Tromsø, by boat from the city.

items.name: Dog sledding
items.why: Drive your own team of huskies through the snowy valleys of Kvaløya or Lyngen.

items.name: Kvaløya and Sommarøy by car
items.why: Mountains straight out of the sea, white beaches and the fishing island of Sommarøy; midnight sun in summer.

areas.season: Called the town of the northern lights, inland and drier than the coast: September to March for the aurora, December to April for snow.
areas.sleep: In town, or the snow hotel at Sorrisniva in winter.

items.name: The rock carvings of Alta
items.why: Over 6,000 figures of reindeer, boats and hunters cut 2,000 to 7,000 years ago, on UNESCO's list; the outdoor paths are open in summer, the museum all year.

items.name: Northern lights
items.why: The dry inland sky of Finnmark gives more clear nights than the coast.

items.name: Reindeer and Sami culture
items.why: Meet reindeer herders, ride a reindeer sled and eat by the fire in a lavvu tent.

items.name: Northern Lights Cathedral
items.why: A titanium spiral of a church, built in 2013 in the shape of the aurora.

areas.season: Cold, short days in winter (5 hours of light in December), mild summers.
areas.sleep: The centre or Bakklandet across the Old Town Bridge.

items.name: Nidaros Cathedral and Bakklandet
items.why: The northernmost medieval cathedral of the world, built over the grave of St Olav, then the wooden warehouses and cafés across the Old Town Bridge.
